info.name: OpenRegister Draft Activation API
info.description:
POST /api/objects/{register}/{schema}/{id}/activate, asserted over HTTP (change draft-owner-activation-and-lifetime, decision 216). A caller's side view, so the DELIVERED status of a refusal is what is checked.

THREE ACCOUNTS: the administrator, the draft's owner and a colleague who is no administrator. Every request carries its own basic auth and sends no cookies (protocolProfileBehavior.disableCookies). With a cookie jar the administrator's session rides along on the owner's requests and Nextcloud answers as the administrator, whatever the Authorization header says: that made this collection's first CI run red, with a draft owned by the administrator. The 'who am I' steps assert that the server sees the account each step names and that the three differ.

WHAT IT ASSERTS, each paired with its control:
  * the administrator, who may read the draft, is refused with a delivered 403; a colleague, who may not, with 404; the draft is still a draft afterwards
  * a colleague cannot change the draft through PATCH, PUT or a POST that names its id, and the answer never holds its content
  * a plain save that sets @self.status to active stays refused, for the owner, the administrator and a colleague, on PUT and on PATCH
  * an incomplete draft is refused with 422 and a `required` finding per property
  * the owner's activation answers 200 with the same id and status active
  * a second activation answers 409, an unknown id 404
  * a schema keeps its draftLifetimeDays on save and on read
  * the owner sees their own draft in a list by default, and _drafts=none leaves it out while the rest stays

The cleanup job is not asserted here: it runs from cron, and its path from appinfo/info.xml to the delete is covered by DraftExpiryJobTest.

item.name: setUp: a second account, who will own the draft

exec: // A draft has one owner, so the refusals need more accounts: the owner, and a colleague who is no administrator. Both are removed in tearDown.
const suffix = Date.now().toString(36) + Math.random().toString(36).slice(2, 8);
const password = () => 'Dr4ft!' + suffix + '-' + Math.random().toString(36).slice(2) + 'Zq9';
pm.collectionVariables.set('ownerId', 'or-draft-owner-' + suffix);
pm.collectionVariables.set('ownerPassword', password());
pm.collectionVariables.set('colleagueId', 'or-draft-colleague-' + suffix);
pm.collectionVariables.set('colleaguePassword', password());
pm.test('the draft owner account is created', () => pm.expect(pm.response.code, pm.response.text()).to.eql(200));

item.name: setUp: a third account, a colleague who is no administrator

exec: pm.test('the colleague account is created', () => pm.expect(pm.response.code, pm.response.text()).to.eql(200));

item.name: GET who am I as the administrator -> each step runs as the account its name claims

exec: // The first run of this collection in CI was red for this reason alone: the cookie jar carried the
// administrator's session into the owner's requests, and Nextcloud answers a request that has a
// session as that session's user, whatever its Authorization header says. So the draft was the
// administrator's, and "somebody else" was its owner. Every request here sends no cookies
// (protocolProfileBehavior.disableCookies), and these steps fail when that stops being true.
pm.test('the request is answered', () => pm.expect(pm.response.code, pm.response.text()).to.eql(200));
const id = String(pm.response.json().ocs.data.id);
pm.test('the server sees the administrator', () => pm.expect(id).to.eql(String(pm.variables.get('admin_user'))));
const accounts = [String(pm.variables.get('admin_user')), String(pm.collectionVariables.get('ownerId')), String(pm.collectionVariables.get('colleagueId'))];
pm.test('the three accounts are three different accounts', () => pm.expect(new Set(accounts).size, accounts.join(', ')).to.eql(3));
pm.test('no account name is empty', () => accounts.forEach((account) => pm.expect(account).to.not.be.oneOf(['', 'undefined', 'null'])));

item.name: setUp: a register

body.raw: {"title": "draft activation newman register", "description": "draft activation collection fixture"}

exec: pm.test('the register is created', () => pm.expect(pm.response.code, pm.response.text()).to.be.below(300));
pm.collectionVariables.set('registerId', String(pm.response.json().id));

item.name: setUp: a schema with two required properties and a draft lifetime

body.raw: {"title": "draft activation newman schema", "description": "draft activation collection fixture", "required": ["subject", "channel"], "properties": {"subject": {"type": "string", "title": "Subject", "maxLength": 200}, "channel": {"type": "string", "title": "Channel", "enum": ["phone", "email", "counter"]}, "note": {"type": "string", "title": "Note"}}, "configuration": {"draftLifetimeDays": 7}, "authorization": {"read": ["authenticated"], "create": ["authenticated"], "update": ["authenticated"], "delete": ["authenticated"]}}

exec: pm.test('the schema is created', () => pm.expect(pm.response.code, pm.response.text()).to.be.below(300));
pm.collectionVariables.set('schemaId', String(pm.response.json().id));

item.name: setUp: the register carries the schema

exec: pm.test('the schema is attached', () => pm.expect(pm.response.code, pm.response.text()).to.be.below(300));

item.name: GET the schema -> the draft lifetime survived the save

exec: pm.test('the schema is readable', () => pm.expect(pm.response.code, pm.response.text()).to.eql(200));
// An unknown configuration key vanishes on save without a word; this one is declared.
pm.test('draftLifetimeDays reads back as 7', () => pm.expect((pm.response.json().configuration || {}).draftLifetimeDays).to.eql(7));

item.name: setUp: the owner starts a draft that misses a required property

exec: pm.test('the draft is created', () => pm.expect(pm.response.code, pm.response.text()).to.be.below(300));
const b = pm.response.json();
pm.collectionVariables.set('draftUuid', String((b['@self'] && b['@self'].id) || b.id || b.uuid));
pm.test('it is a draft', () => pm.expect((b['@self'] || {}).status).to.eql('draft'));
// The stored owner is what the activation compares with, so it is asserted where the draft is made.
pm.test('the draft is the owner account\'s', () => pm.expect((b['@self'] || {}).owner).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get('ownerId')));
pm.test('the draft is not the administrator\'s', () => pm.expect((b['@self'] || {}).owner).to.not.eql(pm.variables.get('admin_user')));

item.name: POST .../activate as the administrator -> 403, delivered as 403

exec: // The administrator may read the draft and is still not its owner. The status is the point:
// OCSMiddleware would deliver a 403 from an OCSController as HTTP 200 with the refusal in the body.
pm.test('the refusal is not delivered as a success', () => pm.expect(pm.response.code, pm.response.text()).to.be.at.least(400));
pm.test('a non-owner is refused with 403', () => pm.expect(pm.response.code, pm.response.text()).to.eql(403));
pm.test('the reason is not-the-owner', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().reason).to.eql('not-the-owner'));

item.name: POST .../activate as a colleague -> 404, the draft does not exist for them

exec: // A colleague may not read somebody else's draft, so it answers as an unknown id does.
pm.test('a colleague is refused with 404', () => pm.expect(pm.response.code, pm.response.text()).to.eql(404));
pm.test('the reason is not-found', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().reason).to.eql('not-found'));

item.name: GET the draft as a colleague -> 404

exec: pm.test('a colleague cannot read the draft', () => pm.expect(pm.response.code, pm.response.text()).to.eql(404));

item.name: PATCH the draft as a colleague -> refused, somebody who cannot read a draft cannot change it

exec: // Found on a live instance, 12 October 2026: this answered 200 with the draft's content.
pm.test('the change is refused', () => pm.expect(pm.response.code, pm.response.text()).to.be.within(400, 499));
pm.test('the answer does not hold the draft', () => pm.expect(pm.response.text()).to.not.include('Bin not collected'));

item.name: POST naming the draft's id as a colleague -> refused, a create cannot land on a draft

exec: pm.test('the write is refused', () => pm.expect(pm.response.code, pm.response.text()).to.be.within(400, 499));
pm.test('the answer does not hold the draft', () => pm.expect(pm.response.text()).to.not.include('Bin not collected'));

item.name: PUT the draft as a colleague -> 404

exec: pm.test('a colleague cannot replace the draft', () => pm.expect(pm.response.code, pm.response.text()).to.be.within(400, 499));

item.name: GET the draft as its owner -> still a draft after the refusals

exec: pm.test('the draft is readable by its owner', () => pm.expect(pm.response.code, pm.response.text()).to.eql(200));
pm.test('it is still a draft', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json()['@self'].status).to.eql('draft'));
pm.test('it is still the owner\'s', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json()['@self'].owner).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get('ownerId')));
pm.test('it holds what its owner typed', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().subject).to.eql('Bin not collected'));
pm.test('nobody filled in the channel', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().channel == null).to.eql(true));

item.name: PUT with @self.status active as the owner -> a plain save cannot leave draft

exec: pm.test('the save is refused', () => pm.expect(pm.response.code, pm.response.text()).to.be.within(400, 499));

item.name: PATCH with @self.status active as the owner -> refused

exec: pm.test('the save is refused for the owner', () => pm.expect(pm.response.code, pm.response.text()).to.be.within(400, 499));

item.name: PUT with @self.status active as the administrator -> refused

exec: pm.test('the save is refused for the administrator', () => pm.expect(pm.response.code, pm.response.text()).to.be.within(400, 499));

item.name: PATCH with @self.status active as the administrator -> refused

exec: pm.test('the save is refused for the administrator', () => pm.expect(pm.response.code, pm.response.text()).to.be.within(400, 499));

item.name: PATCH with @self.status active as a colleague -> refused

exec: pm.test('the save is refused for a colleague', () => pm.expect(pm.response.code, pm.response.text()).to.be.within(400, 499));

item.name: GET the draft as its owner -> still a draft after every plain save

exec: pm.test('the draft is readable by its owner', () => pm.expect(pm.response.code, pm.response.text()).to.eql(200));
pm.test('no plain save left draft', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json()['@self'].status).to.eql('draft'));
pm.test('no refused save stored its channel', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().channel == null).to.eql(true));
pm.test('it holds what its owner typed', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().subject).to.eql('Bin not collected'));

item.name: POST .../activate incomplete -> 422 with a finding per property

exec: pm.test('an incomplete draft is refused with 422', () => pm.expect(pm.response.code, pm.response.text()).to.eql(422));
const body = pm.response.json();
pm.test('the reason is invalid', () => pm.expect(body.reason).to.eql('invalid'));
pm.test('the missing property is named', () => pm.expect((body.findings || []).map((f) => f.property)).to.include('channel'));
pm.test('the finding says required', () => pm.expect(((body.findings || []).find((f) => f.property === 'channel') || {}).code).to.eql('required'));

item.name: POST .../activate with the last value -> 200, active, same id

exec: pm.test('the owner makes the draft definitive', () => pm.expect(pm.response.code, pm.response.text()).to.eql(200));
const b = pm.response.json();
pm.test('the id did not change', () => pm.expect(String((b['@self'] && b['@self'].id) || b.id || b.uuid)).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get('draftUuid')));
pm.test('the status is active', () => pm.expect((b['@self'] || {}).status).to.eql('active'));
pm.test('the last value was saved', () => pm.expect(b.channel).to.eql('phone'));

item.name: GET the object as the administrator -> active

exec: pm.test('the object is readable', () => pm.expect(pm.response.code, pm.response.text()).to.eql(200));
pm.test('it left draft', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json()['@self'].status).to.eql('active'));

item.name: POST .../activate again -> 409, there is no draft left

exec: pm.test('an object that is not a draft answers 409', () => pm.expect(pm.response.code, pm.response.text()).to.eql(409));
pm.test('the reason is not-a-draft', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().reason).to.eql('not-a-draft'));

item.name: POST .../activate on an unknown object -> 404

exec: pm.test('an unknown id answers 404', () => pm.expect(pm.response.code, pm.response.text()).to.eql(404));
pm.test('the reason is not-found', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().reason).to.eql('not-found'));

item.name: setUp: the owner starts a second draft

exec: pm.test('the second draft is created', () => pm.expect(pm.response.code, pm.response.text()).to.be.below(300));
const b = pm.response.json();
pm.collectionVariables.set('secondDraftUuid', String((b['@self'] && b['@self'].id) || b.id || b.uuid));

item.name: GET the list as the owner -> their own draft is in it by default

exec: pm.test('the list is readable', () => pm.expect(pm.response.code, pm.response.text()).to.eql(200));
const ids = (pm.response.json().results || []).map((b) => String((b['@self'] && b['@self'].id) || b.id || b.uuid));
pm.test('the owner sees their own draft by default (decision 201)', () => pm.expect(ids).to.include(pm.collectionVariables.get('secondDraftUuid')));
pm.test('and the activated object', () => pm.expect(ids).to.include(pm.collectionVariables.get('draftUuid')));

item.name: GET the list with _drafts=none -> no drafts, the owner's own included

exec: pm.test('the list is readable', () => pm.expect(pm.response.code, pm.response.text()).to.eql(200));
const ids = (pm.response.json().results || []).map((b) => String((b['@self'] && b['@self'].id) || b.id || b.uuid));
pm.test('the owner\'s own draft is left out', () => pm.expect(ids).to.not.include(pm.collectionVariables.get('secondDraftUuid')));
// Control: the lens hides drafts, it does not empty the list.
pm.test('the activated object is still there', () => pm.expect(ids).to.include(pm.collectionVariables.get('draftUuid')));

item.name: tearDown: the second draft

exec: pm.test('the second draft is removed', () => pm.expect(pm.response.code, pm.response.text()).to.be.below(300));

item.name: tearDown: the object

exec: pm.test('the object is removed', () => pm.expect(pm.response.code, pm.response.text()).to.be.below(300));

item.name: tearDown: the schema

exec: pm.test('the schema delete does not error', () => pm.expect(pm.response.code, pm.response.text()).to.be.below(500));

item.name: tearDown: the register

exec: pm.test('the register delete does not error', () => pm.expect(pm.response.code, pm.response.text()).to.be.below(500));

item.name: tearDown: the second account

exec: pm.test('the draft owner account is removed', () => pm.expect(pm.response.code, pm.response.text()).to.eql(200));

item.name: tearDown: the third account

exec: pm.test('the colleague account is removed', () => pm.expect(pm.response.code, pm.response.text()).to.eql(200));
